The first stop is Ahu Akahanga, where, according to local legend, the island's first king, Hotu Matu'a, is buried.

Next is Rano Raraku, the volcanic quarry where the moai were carved. Dozens of unfinished statues remain on its slopes.

A packed lunch is included.

Afterwards, visit Ahu Tongariki, the largest platform, with 15 restored moai.

Continue to the Poike Peninsula and Ahu Te Pito Kura, home to the island's largest statue.

The day ends at Anakena Beach, with its white sand, palm trees and warm turquoise water.

Return to Hanga Roa. The excursion lasts a full day.

An early overland transfer takes you to a landing upstream. From there, you travel along the Carrao River in motorized indigenous canoes. Along the way, there is a walk across the savanna and a visit to the "Pool of Happiness."

The boats then enter the narrower Churún River and head towards Devil's Canyon. High vertical rock walls rise above the water, with cascades running down their slopes. The route follows the river that receives water from Angel Falls.

Near Ratoncito Island, Angel Falls comes into view. Its waters plunge almost 1,000 metres before crashing onto the rocks below. Next comes a walk of approximately one hour through tropical vegetation, past small orange and red streams, enormous trees covered with orchids and bromeliads, and moss-covered stones.

The trail leads to the Laime viewpoint. After seeing the world's highest waterfall, you will have lunch and return to Canaima. The excursion takes a full day; the order of activities may change depending on the weather and river conditions.

During the boat excursion, you will visit picturesque islands and make several stops at some of their finest beaches. Expect magnificent scenery: white sand, calm, deep-blue waters and numerous scenic islets scattered across the bay.

Heading out to sea offers the chance to see dolphins, sea turtles and rays, and occasionally even whales. You will be able to swim in crystal-clear water and enjoy the surrounding nature.

The excursion takes place without a guide.

Angra dos Reis is a paradise for island lovers, with countless islands and beautiful beaches off its coast.

The boat journey then continues towards Ilha Grande, with views of the picturesque Blue Lagoon along the way.

After breakfast, your driver will pick you up from your hotel in Rio de Janeiro. You will head for the tropical islands and spend the day on a boat around Angra dos Reis and Ilha Grande.

Green hillsides descend to the water, and views of bays and the coastline open up between the islands. The boat trip lets you see this corner of Brazil from the water.

The excursion runs approximately from 10:00 to 16:00. Afterwards, your driver will take you back to your hotel in Rio de Janeiro.

Antigua lies in the Panchoy Valley between the Agua, Acatenango and Fuego volcanoes. Founded in 1543, the city was Guatemala's third capital and was known as Santiago de Guatemala. After the Santa Marta earthquake of 1773, the capital was moved, and the former city came to be known as Antigua, or "old Guatemala." The walk begins in the main square of the historic centre and passes the city's principal monuments.

Next is San Antonio Aguas Calientes, known for its textiles and crafts. In Santiago Zamora, you will meet the Ixoqi group of women artisans and see how traditional techniques are used to make textiles.
